# **01  Brand Foundation**

This guide translates Jasper's founder positioning into a consistent visual system for press, speaking and media use. It is built to read as institutional and credible on first impression, the visual equivalent of a spokesperson who deals in infrastructure, compliance and settlement certainty, not a consumer app.

## **Locked one-liner**

*“I build the orchestration layer for programmable money.”*

## 

## **Brand attributes → visual translation**

| ATTRIBUTE | HOW IT SHOWS UP VISUALLY |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Confident operator** | Structured layouts, generous white space, restrained color use. Nothing crowded or promotional. |
| **Proof-backed** | Numbers and named partners set in the same disciplined type system as everything else, data presented like fact, not marketing. |
| **Independent / neutral** | A palette that is deliberately not card-network blue or crypto neon, ink, graphite and bronze read as infrastructure, not a fintech app. |
| **Institutional trust** | Serif display type for name and headlines (the register of banks, exchanges and financial press), paired with a clean grotesque sans for reading text. |
| **Security-first** | Sharp edges, thin precise rules, monochrome photography grading, a controlled, engineered feel rather than soft or playful. |

# 

# **02  Design Rationale**

Jasper's positioning is built on a security-operator background, an orchestration-layer thesis, and physical-world proof points (the FCTI ATM network, Ordr venues, the NYSE floor interview). The visual identity is designed to carry that story even with no caption attached.

* Deep ink-navy over pure black, reads as institutional and trustworthy without the coldness of true black; distinct from Coinbase blue, Visa blue and generic crypto neon.  
* A single warm-bronze accent stands in for “programmable money made tangible”, precious-metal, settlement, value, used sparingly so it never feels decorative.  
* The orchestration line motif (page 6\) visualizes the one-layer-across-many-rails thesis without needing an explainer.  
* Serif display type signals editorial and financial-press credibility (the register of the Financial Times, The Economist, NYSE materials); the sans keeps everything else efficient and legible at press-kit speed.  
* Photography direction is deliberately closer to a bank CEO or a security researcher than a consumer-startup founder, direct, still, unforced.

 

# **03  Color System**

Five colors, used with discipline. Ink Navy and Bone carry roughly 80% of any application; Bronze is a single accent, never a fill; Graphite handles text; Settlement Blue is reserved for data and never competes with Bronze on the same element.

| SWATCH | NAME / HEX | CMYK (PRINT) | USAGE |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
|   | **Ink Navy \- primary** HEX 0A1628 | CMYK 92 / 76 / 45 / 55 | Backgrounds, wordmark, dominant surface color |
|   | **Signal Bronze \- accent** HEX B4905A | CMYK 0 / 25 / 60 / 20 | Rules, monogram ring, pull-quotes, callouts only |
|   | **Graphite \- secondary** HEX 3A4453 | CMYK 70 / 58 / 45 / 20 | Body copy on light backgrounds, captions, UI chrome |
|   | **Bone \- paper** HEX F5F1E8 | CMYK 3 / 3 / 8 / 0 | Primary light background, print stock reference |
|   | **Settlement Blue \- tertiary** HEX 3A5C9E | CMYK 78 / 55 / 8 / 5 | Charts, links, data highlights, used sparingly, never adjacent to Bronze |

*Print builds: verify CMYK against the specific press/stock before production. Digital builds: use hex values directly.*

## 

## **Pairing rules**

* Navy background \+ Bone/White text, or Bone background \+ Navy/Graphite text. Never navy text on graphite, never bronze text on bone (fails contrast for print/AA).  
* Bronze appears once per composition, a rule, a monogram ring, a single pull-quote mark. Two bronze elements in one layout reads as decorative, not premium.  
* Settlement Blue is for charts and hyperlinks only; it never appears in the logo lockup or headline type.

 

# **04  Typography**

A two-family system: an editorial serif for the name, headlines and pull-quotes; a clean grotesque sans for everything functional, body copy, captions, data, UI.

## **Display serif (Cambria \- headlines, name lockup, pull-quotes)**

*Recommended: GT Sectra Display / Canela / Freight Display*  
*Built-in substitute: Georgia (Word/press-kit compatible fallback used throughout this document)*

**Programmable Money, Orchestrated**

## **Body sans \- text, captions, data, UI**

*Recommended: Söhne / Inter / Neue Haas Grotesk*  
*Built-in substitute: Calibri*

“We connect programmable money to the places people actually spend it.”

## **Type scale**

| Display | 32 pt | Jasper Fu |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **H1** | 24 pt | **The Orchestration Layer** |
| **H2** | 18 pt | **Programmable Money** |
| **Body** | 11 pt | Rail-agnostic, plug-and-play infrastructure. |
| **Caption** | 9 pt | Co-Founder & CEO, CoinSub |

*Letterspacing: display serif set at 0–10 tracking; sans-serif kickers (section labels, eyebrows) set at \+30 tracking, uppercase, bronze or navy only.*

 

# **05  Logo & Monogram**

The primary mark for press and speaking use is a wordmark: “JASPER FU” set in the display serif, all caps, wide tracking. The JF monogram (below) is the secondary mark, for avatars, favicons, name badges and the press-kit header where a wordmark won't fit.

![][image1] ![][image2]  ![][image3]

*JF monogram \- ink navy field, bone lettering, single bronze ring. Never filled solid bronze; never placed on a photographic background without a solid-color plate behind it.*

## 

## **Clear space & minimum size**

* Clear space: maintain padding equal to the height of the “J” on all sides, no text, edge or photography inside that margin.  
* Minimum size: 28px / 0.3" diameter for the monogram; below that, drop to initials-only in plain type rather than shrinking the ring.

## **Do / don't**

* Do place the monogram on Ink Navy, Bone, or a solid photograph shadow area with sufficient contrast.  
* Don't recolor the ring to Settlement Blue, don't add drop shadows or bevels, don't stretch or rotate the mark.

 

# **06  Graphic Motif \- The Orchestration Line**

A recurring line-and-node graphic represents the thesis in one glance: independent rails (stablecoin, crypto, fiat) resolving through a single neutral layer. Used as a section divider, a footer element, or a subtle background treatment, never as decoration for its own sake.

![][image4]  
*Rail lines in muted bronze and settlement blue; nodes and connective path in bone. Reduce to a single flat rule (page dividers, this document) when full motif is too busy.*

## **Where it appears**

* Press-kit and website section dividers  
* Title slide / closing slide of any keynote deck  
* Footer strip on one-pagers and the fact sheet  
* Never on the monogram, never behind body text, never as a repeating pattern/wallpaper


# **07  Photography Direction**

Photography should read as editorial financial press, not startup marketing: still, direct, engineered. The existing NYSE-floor / Jane King interview is the benchmark asset, trading-floor and institutional backdrops, structured tailoring, direct gaze, natural expression rather than a performed smile.  
![][image5]  
*Framing guide: head on the upper third-line, eyes on the horizontal third, shoulders anchoring the base, consistent crop across headshots, keynote thumbnails and the press kit.*

## 

## **Direction**

* Settings: trading floors, glass-and-steel institutional interiors, minimal studio sets in Ink Navy or Graphite. Avoid casual startup-office backdrops (bean bags, exposed brick, ping-pong tables).  
* Wardrobe: structured, tailored, dark tones (navy, charcoal, ink) with minimal pattern, reads as operator, not founder-casual.  
* Grading: desaturated, cool-neutral, slightly lifted blacks, closer to a broadsheet financial-press photo than a warm consumer-brand tone.  
* Expression: composed and direct-to-camera for headshots; natural mid-conversation for interview/B-roll stills.

## 

## **Avoid**

* Ring-light selfie style, phone-camera candids for any press-facing us  
* Crypto-visual clichés, neon gradients, glowing coins, matrix-code overlays  
* Busy or branded backdrops that compete with the subject

 

# **08  Voice-to-Visual Alignment**

The terminology guardrails from Jasper's positioning summary map directly onto the visual system, so the language and the look reinforce the same story.

| SAY | VISUAL EQUIVALENT |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Orchestration layer** | The line motif, many rails resolving into one path |
| **Rail-agnostic / independent** | Neutral navy palette, deliberately outside card-network or crypto color codes |
| **Settlement certainty** | Precise grid, aligned rules, no loose or floating elements |
| **Security \+ compliance lens** | Sharp edges, restrained color, engineered rather than decorative |
| **Co-founder voice** | Layouts built to hold two names/photos at equal visual weight when needed |

# **09  Applications**

How the system assembles across the founder press-website build and standard media touchpoints.

## 

## **Press / media kit header**

* Ink Navy band, Bone wordmark, monogram top-left, single bronze rule beneath, headshots, boilerplate and fact sheet follow immediately below.

## 

## **Website hero**

* Bone background, Navy display-serif headline (the locked one-liner), thin orchestration-line rule, single high-contrast editorial photo right-aligned.

## 

## **One-pager / fact sheet**

* Navy header band with monogram, Bone body, proof points set as a simple bordered table (see Section 3 style) rather than icons or infographics.

## 

## **Slide template (keynotes, panels)**

* Title and closing slides: full Navy field, Bone type, motif reduced to a single footer line. Content slides: Bone field, Navy/Graphite text, bronze used only for the current section's kicker label.

## 

## **Social / speaker-card banner**

* Navy field, monogram \+ name lockup, one proof point (e.g. the FCTI or Ordr line) set in the sans caption style, no gradients, no stock icons.

## 

## **Email signature**

* Plain-text hierarchy: Name (bold sans) / Title (regular) / one boilerplate line / press contact, no colored banners or embedded logos that break in mail clients.

 

# **10  Usage Guidelines**

## 

## **Always**

* Keep Ink Navy and Bone as the dominant surfaces on any asset.  
* Use the locked one-liner exactly as written wherever a tagline is needed.  
* Hold equal visual weight for David Akers where the asset represents the co-founder story, per the v2 collaborative-voice guardrail.

## 

## **Never**

* Introduce a second accent color alongside Bronze in the same composition.  
* Use crypto-visual clichés (neon, glow, coin iconography, matrix code).  
* Stretch, recolor, rotate or add effects to the monogram or wordmark.  
* Pair Bronze text directly on Graphite or Navy-on-Navy, check contrast before publishing.

# 

# **11  Appendix \- Asset Checklist**

* Monogram: full-color (Navy/Bone/Bronze), single-color Navy, single-color Bone/reversed \- PNG \+ SVG  
* Wordmark lockup: horizontal and stacked versions \- PNG \+ SVG  
* Headshots: color \+ B\&W, web (72dpi) \+ print (300dpi) resolution, per the Section 7 crop guide  
* Orchestration-line motif: full graphic \+ single-rule reduction, both in Navy-background and Bone-background versions  
* Color palette swatch file (Section 3\) for design handoff \- hex \+ CMYK  
* Type specimen sheet (Section 4\) for any external designer or agency brief
